skin.setting: a village inn on a wet night
skin.title: A Night at the Fleece
skin.place: the Fleece, a small inn on the London road
skin.styleGuide: Lamplit interiors, wet slate and brick, brown and ochre, a low ceiling.

rooms.name: the Taproom
rooms.description: The public room, and where the body was found.

rooms.name: the Kitchen
rooms.description: The range, the back stairs, and the door to the yard.

rooms.name: the Parlour
rooms.description: The small room kept for guests who pay for quiet.

rooms.name: the Back Yard
rooms.description: Barrels, the pump, and a gate nobody uses after dark.

people.name: Ruth Calder
people.bio: Has kept the Fleece eleven years and knows to the penny what it owes.
people.voice: Short, level, and never the first to speak.
people.motive: The brewery was about to take the licence off her.
people.portrait: A woman of fifty with grey hair pinned back tightly, a square face, dark eyes, a plain high-necked dress. Composed and watchful.

people.name: Tom Pike
people.bio: Nineteen, strong, and slower to answer than he is to understand.
people.voice: Eager, over-explains, calls everyone sir or missus.
people.motive: She had promised him the tenancy and then not mentioned it again.
people.portrait: A young man of nineteen, broad-shouldered, close-cropped fair hair, a round open face, a collarless shirt. Earnest.

people.name: Alice Verity
people.bio: Came in off the London coach and asked for the parlour.
people.voice: Precise, a little amused, answers exactly what was asked.
people.motive: She had come a long way to speak to the dead man.
people.portrait: A woman of about thirty-five, dark hair under a travelling hat, a narrow intelligent face, a grey coat. Calm and alert.

people.name: Edward Mainwaring
people.bio: Came to settle an account and did not leave.
people.portrait: A heavy man of fifty in a good dark overcoat, side-whiskers, a florid face. Pleased with himself.

silence: I've told you what I know about that.
Couldn't say, missus. I wasn't minding.
I'm afraid I have nothing to offer you there.
skin.briefing: Edward Mainwaring came to the Fleece to settle an account, and he did not leave it. He was found in the taproom when the house was shut up for the night. The surgeon will commit himself no further than this: the man died between nine and ten o'clock. Three people were under this roof that evening, and one of them was alone with him when it happened.
skin.scene: The taproom of a small English inn at night, empty, lamps still lit, chairs pushed back from the tables, rain against the black windows.
skin.summingUp: Ruth Calder came in out of her own yard at ten o'clock, and she is the only one of the three who could have been in that room at that hour. It was never a question of who had a reason to want him gone. Every one of them had that. It was a question of who had the hour.
